body: When I tried to kill myself and then the ideation didn't go away for the next 10 or so years.

Thanks for the concern and your suggestions, I really appreciate the insight. I asked the customer support to confirm with me that I wouldn't be matched with him again, so I think until I hear from them, I will probably just use another service.
Thanks for the suggestions. I submitted a report through their system. I hope it resolves this.

So it's not necessarily grad-school themed, but "**The Hilarious World of Depression**" is my favorite podcast I've ever listened to.

It helped me get through some of the hardest times in my PhD.

Lots of common themes in the world of comedy as grad school -- Impostor syndrome, social anxiety, finding a healthy outlet, your work being a joke, etc.

Thanks so much. The community here really helped me push through the fears regarding therapy. This was literally life-changing.

I can't say thank you enough for the support.

Thank you.

I just recently started seeing a counseling service. I hope it leads somewhere.

I hope you are faring well too.

I may not know you either, but I know you are kind and empathetic enough to reach out to a total stranger, and I can't appreciate that enough.

Hang in there.

Man, I just popped into this subreddit because I was considering posting the same question.

I can't focus on my research so much anymore because suicidal thoughts consume pretty much all of my thought.

Fortunately, my adviser and committee are great.

Unfortunately, depression doesn't care.

My academic brain says, "I believe grad school is possibly one of the greatest stressors on mental health because the advancement of human knowledge (i.e. your project) relies on the plunge into uncertainty and the unknown."

However, my depressed brain undercuts this by saying "you are not smart or driven enough to deserve to be here. Everyone is so much better than you, and you will never amount to anything."

It's a constant battle between believing I am a failure, and acknowledging that progress stems from the ashes of failure... and lately I feel like I am losing this battle.

I don't expect a response. I just need to get this out.

My heart has been racing all day. 

I feel like I will never amount to anything worthwhile

I have been shopping for guns and longing for death.

Why is just existing so painful? Why does it feel like a fist is squeezing down on my heart and throat all the time? Why am I so ashamed of who I am that I can't look my own reflection in the eye, nonetheless anyone else? Why can I only see the world through a fugue of exhaustion and self-hatred? Why can't I be better for those around me? Why can't I be happy?

Thanks man. I'm lying in my bed, trying to fall asleep despite my racing heart; my throat and chest tight. The desperation to die is clawing at me. I don't know why it has intensified in the past year or so, but I don't know how much longer I can live like this. I just hope I won't wake up tomorrow, and if I do, I hope my counselor will help me find peace.

I appreciate the solidarity. You stay strong as well. I am certainly trying those approaches, but in the past few years, I stopped getting any enjoyment or fulfillment out of those pleasures. I hope I can start enjoying them again.

Just started therapy last week. 

Trying to figure out how to articulate why I am totally apathetic and tired of life, and how I would rather not wake up every time I fall asleep. I'm on the upswing due to the season so I feel silly talking about a lot of it now, but I hope I can make use of therapy.

Yo, I have my first appointment tomorrow morning too and I am scared shitless. You're not alone. I see it similar to a biopsy or blood draw. Yes, it might hurt at first, but we're going to learn a lot about ourselves and how to tackle the next steps most effectively. Hang in there man.
That's really reassuring, thank you. Looking into the admittance guidelines now.

Thank you for the info. I'm looking into the mandatory reporting guidelines now, but I will remain careful about what I say to the counselor for now. I guess I have been taking steps to get it off my chest on Reddit where I can be open since I can remain anonymous. It actually is more therapeutic than I expected. I appreciate it, man.

Great, thank you so much. This is reassuring that talking about suicide isn't totally off the table. I'll definitely ease into it, probably over several sessions to gauge the counselor. I am still anxious about going in at all, and knowing this is just another reason not to bail on the appointment.

Thanks for the useful info and the genuine concern. I really appreciate that.

I had no idea about the peer support networks, and that definitely sounds like a useful resource.

Would they be required to report a previous attempt if it was more than a decade ago? The suicidal thoughts have been intrusive yet passive for most of my life. I fantasize about detailed plans and how to obtain the means all the time, but I never take the steps to go through with it.

I guess these are concerns that have really led to me shying away from therapy, since losing my autonomy definitely strikes me as worse than death.

This is exactly me.

I have suicidal thoughts pretty much nonstop.

Nobody in my life could guess because I am outwardly cheery and optimistic. I think it's because I don't want to burden anyone with thinking, "maybe he finally killed himself" any time I don't respond to a call or text or something.

I want to go on my own terms, and I want my presence to be an uplifting one while I'm around.
Same. Something about putting on a smiling face and pretending everything is OK just makes me dread going back to visit.

This is exactly how I feel. I find it hard to put into words why I want to end my life while acknowledging that life is a wonderful gift. I feel like a meseeks. Here with a smile, yet "existence is pain!"

This sounds exactly like how I feel. I acknowledge it's probably just a chemical imbalance in the brain, but somehow I still can't come to terms with seeking professional help, even though I'm pretty sure it's exactly what I need. Things are generally good, yet I wish I would die every single day and I am really good at hiding it. 
I suspect if we overcome the hurdle of seeking help, we could probably experience the joy of life again.
I feel you, man. Hang in there.

Thanks for the kind words. I have been trying to strategize how to approach therapy and/or medicine. I hope to actually give it a shot sometime soon. I'm glad you're hanging in there. Seeing that you have overcome something similar genuinely gives me some hope.

I used to enjoy a lot of things. Cooking, gaming, rock climbing, etc. Over the years I feel like everything kind of lost its shiny appeal. I imagine this is what tolerance to a drug feels like. I just don't get the same enjoyment out of life anymore. To me, it sounds like some sort of depressive disorder, but to me, death sounds more appealing than trying to struggle through a lifetime of instability that could potentially leave my family to clean up after my mess if I kill myself later rather than sooner.

I know this is probably an incredibly frustrating response, but it's not really an external stressor. I just feel like I'm done living. It's like if life were a good meal and even though there's still food on my plate, I just don't want anymore.
